theme: Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
queries_run: common crawl columnar index athena query github travel
common crawl host graph rank github dataset
github search: common crawl hotel dataset (blocked, 429)

candidates.name: cdx_toolkit
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library + `cdxt` CLI that unifies querying Common Crawl's per-crawl CDX indices AND the Internet Archive Wayback Machine CDX API behind one interface. Can iterate captures across all Common Crawl monthly crawls for a URL/domain pattern, do size estimation, and pull matching WARC records to local WARC/JSONL/CSV. Apache-2.0, 287 commits, actively maintained.
candidates.why_useful: This is the direct successor/complement to the CDX capture already in hand (2.08M rows over airbnb.com, 50 crawls). Using cdx_toolkit against the Wayback CDX API (not just CC) would let us pull historical archived airbnb.com and AirDNA market pages point-in-time (gap 17, and supports gap 1/2 by finding old cached listing/price pages) without any new scraping infrastructure -- it is a public, ToS-neutral archive read, not a live site scrape.
candidates.time_coverage: Whatever crawls/snapshots exist in CC (2008-present) and Wayback (1996-present)
candidates.size_hint: tool, not a fixed dataset; output size depends on query
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: extends the existing CC CDX capture over airbnb.com; the Wayback-API half is new capability we do not have

candidates.name: warcio
candidates.what_it_holds: Standalone Python library for reading/writing WARC 1.0/1.1 (and ARC) files, streaming, S3/HTTP remote reads, CLI for indexing/validating/recompressing/extracting payloads. Part of the Webrecorder project. Apache-2.0, 161 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Needed to actually open/parse the 3,000 WARC renders we already captured (or any new ones pulled via cdx_toolkit) without standing up Spark; low-friction way to extract page text/HTML from archived Airbnb, AirDNA, or competitor pages for point-in-time price/availability text mining.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: complements existing 3,000 WARC renders already captured

candidates.name: cc-index-table
candidates.what_it_holds: Official tooling to build/query the Common Crawl columnar (Parquet/ORC) URL index. Includes CCIndex2Table, CCIndexExport, CCIndexWarcExport (Java), Docker support, and example SQL for AWS Athena / SparkSQL / Hive covering domain, language, MIME-type and content queries across the full crawl archive (not just one host). Apache-2.0.
candidates.why_useful: Lets us re-run the airbnb.com CDX capture at much larger scale/lower cost via serverless Athena SQL instead of the raw CDX API, and could be pointed at competitor domains (booking.com, vrbo.com, expedia.com, vacasa.com) to build comparable historical URL-presence panels for gap 9 (competitor supply) cheaply.
candidates.size_hint: tool; underlying columnar index is multi-TB on S3 (public, requester-pays for compute only)

candidates.name: cc-pyspark
candidates.what_it_holds: Example PySpark jobs to process CC WARC/WAT/WET at scale: HTML tag frequency, server identification, IP extraction, word/doc frequency, link extraction and web-graph construction, plus SQL querying of the columnar index. MIT license, 157 commits, Python 3.9+/Spark 3.2+.
candidates.why_useful: Base framework for any large-scale reprocessing of Common Crawl WARC data touching travel sites (e.g., extracting hotel/listing counts, price mentions, or link graphs to competitor sites) beyond the single-host capture we already have.

candidates.name: cc-webgraph
candidates.what_it_holds: Tools (PySpark + LAW WebGraph framework) to build host-level and domain-level web graphs from Common Crawl and compute PageRank / Harmonic Centrality rank scores per domain; outputs `*-ranks.txt.gz` files. Apache-2.0, 113 stars, 176 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A free, Common-Crawl-native alternative to Tranco/CrUX for a web-popularity time series on airbnb.com vs booking.com/expedia.com/vrbo.com -- directly targets gap 5 (web-traffic-estimate / rank proxies) and gap 19 (bot/crawler-visible presence) without any paid Similarweb-type feed. Ranks are released per crawl (roughly monthly/bi-monthly), so a multi-year vintage series is buildable by re-downloading historical rank releases.
candidates.time_coverage: each CC crawl since ~2017 has a released host/domain rank file
candidates.size_hint: rank files gzip several hundred MB for full web; can filter to a domain watch-list

candidates.name: cc-crawl-statistics
candidates.what_it_holds: Scripts (crawlstats.py, crawlplot.py) plus PUBLISHED per-crawl statistics (aggregated ~1MiB files + plots at commoncrawl.github.io/cc-crawl-statistics/) covering every monthly crawl from CC-MAIN-2008-2009 to present: page/URL/document counts by host, domain, TLD, MIME type, protocol (HTTP vs HTTPS share), and content language (since mid-2018). Apache-2.0, 317 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Gives a long, free, point-in-time-stamped (one file per monthly crawl, never revised) time series of overall web-crawl composition -- e.g., domain counts, HTTPS adoption, language mix -- useful as a macro internet-activity control variable, and the published files are themselves already a historical vintage register (each crawl's stats file is dated and never overwritten), which is exactly the kind of point-in-time discipline gap 4 wants, even though the subject is the whole web rather than ABNB-specific.
candidates.time_coverage: CC-MAIN-2008-2009 through current monthly crawl (~17 years)
candidates.size_hint: per-crawl aggregate files ~1MiB compressed each, dozens of crawls published

candidates.name: cc-index-server
candidates.what_it_holds: Deployable pywb-based CDX Server + replay index server for Common Crawl collections; installable via pip or Docker with `install-collections.sh` to stand up a local CDX Server API (e.g. `/CC-MAIN-2015-06-index?url=...`) against S3-hosted crawl indices.
candidates.why_useful: Self-hosted alternative to hitting the public CC CDX API when doing larger point-in-time pulls for airbnb.com or competitor domains across many crawls, avoiding public rate limits during a repeated vintage-register build.
candidates.license: unspecified in fetched content (likely Apache-2.0, forked from pywb)
candidates.last_activity: 50 commits, some open issues -- lower activity than core CC repos

candidates.name: news-crawl
candidates.what_it_holds: Apache StormCrawler-based crawler that discovers articles via RSS/Atom feeds and Google News sitemaps and archives full article WARC content, feeding an ongoing AWS Open Dataset ('CC-NEWS') hosted by Common Crawl. Apache-2.0, 204 commits, actively maintained.
candidates.why_useful: CC-NEWS is a continuously updated, free, full-text news-article WARC corpus; filterable for Airbnb/short-term-rental/hospitality news mentions or regulation-tracker source articles (gap 12, gap 14 text/news) without needing a bespoke news scraper -- complements GDELT-style approaches.
candidates.geography: global, multi-language news sources with sitemaps/feeds
candidates.size_hint: CC-NEWS dataset is multi-TB overall; crawler repo itself is code only

candidates.name: waybackpack
candidates.what_it_holds: Pure-Python (single dependency: requests) CLI to bulk-download every Wayback Machine snapshot of a given URL/URL pattern within a date range into timestamped local directories. MIT, 3.2k stars, 114 commits, 213 forks.
candidates.why_useful: Simplest available tool to pull the full history of specific archived pages -- e.g. an AirDNA city market page, an Airbnb newsroom/press page, or a competitor pricing page -- as a time series of snapshots, directly serving gap 17 (Wayback Machine tooling for archived AirDNA/airbnb.com pages).
candidates.time_coverage: whatever the Wayback Machine holds for a given URL (often 2005-present for popular pages)
candidates.last_activity: 3.2k stars, ongoing community engagement (31 open issues)

candidates.name: wayback (OpenWayback / Internet Archive)
candidates.what_it_holds: Internet Archive's own Wayback Machine server implementation, including `wayback-cdx-server` (the reference CDX query server), `wayback-core`, and `wayback-webapp`. 2,983 commits, 120 open issues, 18 open PRs.
candidates.why_useful: Reference implementation for the CDX API that both cdx_toolkit and waybackpack talk to; useful mainly as documentation of the CDX query surface (date-range, collapse, filter params) if we ever need to hand-roll a point-in-time Wayback pull for AirDNA/Airbnb press pages.
candidates.license: not stated in fetched content (historically Apache-2.0 via OpenWayback lineage)

candidates.name: EDGI web-monitoring (Scanner)
candidates.what_it_holds: Multi-repo suite (Python/Ruby/React/Kubernetes) that captures historical snapshots of web pages (importing from Internet Archive among other sources), diffs them, scores which diffs are 'meaningful' vs noise, and surfaces changes for review. CC-BY-SA-4.0 docs, GPLv3 code, 114 stars, running since 2017.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made change-detection pipeline (not just raw snapshot download) that could be pointed at STR-regulation pages (city ordinance sites, gap 12) or AirDNA/competitor pricing pages to flag exactly when content changed between archive captures, cutting manual point-in-time diff work.
candidates.time_coverage: 2017-present monitoring runs; can import older IA snapshots
candidates.geography: originally US federal/government sites, but generic tooling

candidates.name: cc-notebooks
candidates.what_it_holds: Jupyter notebooks demonstrating CC index analysis: domain coverage 2013-2019, character-set/MIME-type stats, a case study on internet-blocking effects visible in the 2019 Iran crawl, WARC exploration via AWS EMR, payload-truncation analysis, and Hugging Face access examples. Apache-2.0, 28 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Worked examples for pulling domain-level coverage metrics year-by-year, which is the template we'd reuse to build an airbnb.com / booking.com / vrbo.com domain-presence panel from the columnar index rather than writing that from scratch; low novelty on its own (no ABNB-specific data).
candidates.size_hint: notebook code only, no bundled dataset

candidates.name: Tranco top-sites list
candidates.what_it_holds: Research-grade top-1M-sites domain ranking aggregated from Cisco Umbrella, Majestic, Farsight, Chrome UX Report (CrUX), and Cloudflare Radar, averaged over rolling 30-day windows; historical daily list IDs are permanently retrievable (point-in-time by construction), with Python/Go client libraries and a GitHub source repo (linked from the site) plus BigQuery access. Not Common-Crawl-derived, but sits in the same 'host popularity ranking' space as cc-webgraph and is more directly comparable to Similarweb/CrUX-rank asks in gap 5.
candidates.why_useful: Gives a genuinely point-in-time (dated list IDs, never revised) domain-popularity series for airbnb.com vs booking.com/expedia.com/vrbo.com going back years, filling gap 5's 'Tranco / host-graph rank' ask directly and with an off-the-shelf client.
candidates.time_coverage: Tranco lists generated daily since ~2018, each permanently archived by ID
candidates.size_hint: each list ~1M domains, small compressed CSV per date
candidates.license: list data CC-BY-4.0-style research use per Tranco's academic paper (verify on repo); client code license per its own GitHub repo

notes: WebSearch tool errored out at start of this session ('budget of 200 already used' -- shared/session-wide limit exhausted by other concurrent scouts before I ran any query), so all findings here came from direct WebFetch on known/guessed GitHub URLs (cocrawler/cdx_toolkit, webrecorder/warcio, the commoncrawl org's own repos, github.com/topics/common-crawl) plus a couple of dead ends (github.com/search?q=... returned HTTP 429 -- GitHub's own search UI rate-limits WebFetch; github.com/commoncrawl/ip-address-visualization and github.com/wumpus/troll-a were 404 -- likely renamed/removed, troll-a shows on the topics page under a different owner I did not chase further). No repo found that mirrors a travel-site-specific dataset already extracted FROM Common Crawl (e.g., a pre-built hotel-price or listing corpus) -- everything genuinely CC-native is generic tooling (cdx_toolkit, warcio, cc-index-table, cc-pyspark, cc-webgraph, cc-crawl-statistics, news-crawl, cc-index-server, cc-notebooks); the travel-relevant candidates are all 'apply this tool to airbnb.com/competitor domains yourself' rather than a committed dataset already keyed to travel. Wayback-Machine-adjacent tools (waybackpack, internetarchive/wayback, EDGI web-monitoring) are the strongest lead for gap 17's 'archived AirDNA market pages' ask since CC's own crawl frequency/coverage of niche STR-data sites like AirDNA is likely thin -- the Wayback Machine has broader incidental coverage. Tranco is not Common-Crawl-derived but is the closest off-the-shelf answer to the 'host-graph rank' half of this theme's brief and directly targets gap 5, so I included it. Given more WebSearch budget I would have chased: cc-net (Facebook's CC pipeline), OSCAR/ungoliant corpus for language-classified web text, and a search for academic replication packages citing Common Crawl for hospitality/tourism NLP (e.g., hotel-review or travel-intent classification papers) which likely exist on Zenodo/HuggingFace but I could not confirm without WebSearch or a working GitHub search page.
